cohort: 7512 pregnancies in 4015 women with CHD, compared to 11,225 pregnancies in 6502 age-matched women without CHD
finding: Women with CHD had a higher rate of caesarean deliveries, maternal complications (stroke, heart failure, and cardiac arrhythmias), and neonatal morbidity/mortality compared to women without CHD.
mod_finding: The study found that cesarean deliveries were more common in pregnant women with congenital heart disease compared to a non-CHD control group.
birth_weight: Mentioned as an outcome, but no specific values provided
